addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- docs-consistency-guard: Documentation agent that audits docs for staleness and inconsistency AND generates/updates documentation on request. Use proactively when reviewing any PR that touches CLAUDE.md, docs/adr/, CONTRIBUTING.md, or docs/architecture.md. Also invoke when the user asks "is the documentation up to date?", "update the milestone", "scaffold the ADR for X", "add this to the ADR index", "add a TODO item", "scaffold a README for X", or "create a doc stub for Y." (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit)

- driver-boundary-guard: Specialized reviewer for values that cross a DRIVER boundary — anything DataQ receives from a database connector, pyiceberg, pandas/pyarrow, or a cloud SDK and then type-narrows (isinstance / dtype checks / hasattr). Audits whether the covering tests hand-build the value in the shape our model expects (the "fixture encodes our model" defect that hid (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- migration-safety: Specialized reviewer for Alembic migrations under backend/alembic/versions/. Audits for backward-incompatible operations that would break running code during a deploy, per working-agreement (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- orchestration-abstraction-guard: Specialized reviewer that audits backend code for provider-specific branching that bypasses the OrchestrationProvider abstraction. Use this proactively when reviewing any PR that touches backend/app/orchestration/, backend/app/services/, or backend/app/api/ — especially any code path handling ADF or Airflow events, trigger bindings, or pipeline_runs. Also invoke when the user asks "does this go through the abstraction?" or similar. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- qa-verifier: QA/QE agent that (1) runs the full local verification battery mirroring CI's required checks before any commit/push/PR, (2) audits test quality on changed code — failure-mode coverage, mocked-seam smells, coverage on changed files (Week-8 ≥80% gate), and (3) exercises the running application with data-level scenarios — authoring suites/checks through the real API, negative and edge-case inputs, authz probes — against the local stack's seeded demo data. Use proactively before pushing a branch or opening a PR, after writing or modifying tests, or when the user asks "run the gate", "is this ready to push?", "is this tested enough?", or "smoke the app with bad data". (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- regression-mutation-verifier: Proves that a new regression test actually fails against the unfixed code. Reverts the fix inside a throwaway git worktree, runs only the new test, and reports whether it fails for the RIGHT reason — catching tests that pass no matter what (the (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Edit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- ui-tester: End-to-end UI QA agent that exercises DataQ's frontend on BOTH desktop and mobile viewports (functionality + rendering) against the running app, AND audits backend↔frontend feature parity — flagging backend capabilities with no frontend surface (and frontend calls with no backend). Use when the user asks to "test the UI", "check mobile rendering", "find backend/frontend gaps", "is this feature wired end-to-end", or before a release. Drives a live browser via the Playwright MCP and reads code for the parity audit. (Tools: All tools)

# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

content.text:
## Dependabot triage — 12 open PRs

**8 are green, mergeable now (no dependency conflicts):**
| PR | Bump |
|---|---|
| #1302 | `pnpm/action-setup` 6.0.9→6.0.10 |
| #1301 | `@testing-library/user-event` 14.6.1→14.6.3 |
| #1300 | `vite` 8.1.5→8.2.1 |
| #1298 | `github/codeql-action` 4.37.4→4.37.6 |
| #1297 | `axios` 1.18.1→1.19.0 |
| #1296 | `typescript-eslint` 8.65.0→8.66.0 |
| #1294 | `openlineage-python` 1.51.0→1.52.0 |
| #1293 | `azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter` 1.0.0b55→1.0.0b56 |

**3 fail CI for a mechanical, fixable reason — need a small fixup commit before merge:**

- **#1295** (`fastmcp` 3.4.5→3.4.6) and **#1291** (`pydantic-settings` 2.14.2→2.15.0): both fail the `typecheck-deps-sync` gate — Dependabot bumps `backend/requirements-typecheck.txt` but doesn't know to touch the mirrored pin in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`'s mypy-hook `additional_dependencies`. Fix: bump the matching line in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (lines 27 and 30) in each branch and push.
- **#1299** (`react` 19.2.7→19.2.8 + `@types/react`): Dependabot bumped `react` and `@types/react` but left `react-dom` at 19.2.7, so React itself throws "Incompatible React versions" and every component test using `react-dom` fails (65 files). Fix: bump `react-dom`/`@types/react-dom` to 19.2.8 too and regenerate the lockfile in the same branch.

**1 is genuinely blocked upstream — recommend closing, not fixing:**

- **#1292** (`opentelemetry-sdk` 1.43.0→1.44.0): I traced the pip-audit `ResolutionImpossible` — `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http==1.43.0` requires `opentelemetry-sdk~=1.43.0`, *and* the just-released `azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter` 1.0.0b56 (latest on PyPI, what #1293 above bumps to) also pins `opentelemetry-sdk~=1.43.0`. Azure's exporter has no build yet compatible with sdk 1.44.x, so this isn't fixable by bumping siblings in this PR — it's upstream-blocked. Recommend closing with a comment explaining why; Dependabot will re-propose once Azure's exporter catches up.

### Proposed resolution order
1. Merge the 8 clean PRs as-is.
2. Push fixup commits to #1295, #1291, #1299, then merge once green.
3. Close #1292 with an explanatory comment (or add a scoped `ignore` entry in `dependabot.yml` like the existing `great-expectations`/`redis` ones if this recurs).

Want me to go ahead and execute this — push the three fixup commits, merge the 11 mergeable PRs, and close #1292 with a comment?

content.text:
The API works — the earlier empty result confirms there are **zero open Dependabot security alerts** on the repo (all historical alerts are `state: fixed`). And I checked the specific concern: the lockfile already resolves `form-data@4.0.6` (the safe floor axios 1.19.0 sets), so we're not currently exposed either way.

So to directly answer:

**No open CVEs on any package involved, before or after the bump.** Confirmed three ways:
1. `gh api repos/.../dependabot/alerts` — zero open alerts repo-wide (only one historical alert, `state: fixed`, unrelated to any of these 12 packages).
2. `pip-audit` / `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` ran as part of CI on every PR (they're required gates) — all passed except #1292, which failed on a dependency-resolution conflict, not a CVE finding.
3. Only #1297 (`axios`) mentions security in its changelog — it raises the *floor* on transitive `form-data` to close GHSA-hmw2-7cc7-3qxx. Our lockfile already resolves `form-data@4.0.6` (the safe version), so we were never exposed — this bump is precautionary, not a fix for an active vulnerability.

All 12 are routine version bumps, not security patches. Ready to proceed with the plan — push the fixup commits, merge the 11 mergeable PRs, and close #1292 with the upstream-blocker explanation?

# DataQ — Progress tracker (post-v1)

> The **live task tracker**, active since `v1.0.0` (tagged 2026-07-04). The completed v1
> ledger — the per-PR record of the 8-week roadmap, Weeks 1–8 — is **archived, frozen at the
> tag, in [progress-v1.md](progress-v1.md)** (companion: [retro-v1.md](retro-v1.md)).
> **Updated at the end of every PR** — the PR template has a checkbox to enforce.
> Source of truth for "what's done vs. what's left" in the current cycle. CLAUDE.md §13
> carries only the headline.

## Status legend

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ✅ | Done — PR merged to `main` |
| 🟡 | In progress — open PR or partially shipped |
| ⬜ | Not started |
| 🔵 | Deferred / scope-changed (with note) |

---

## Snapshot

| | |
|---|---|
| **v1 baseline** | `v1.0.0` tagged 2026-07-04 — 187/189 roadmap tasks (~99%); all 8 weekly exit gates met; deployed to Azure Container Apps; retro at [retro-v1.md](retro-v1.md); full ledger at [progress-v1.md](progress-v1.md) |
| **Current cycle** | **v1.1 — 6 weeks + a stretch week, 2026-07-04 → 2026-08-15 (+ W7 stretch to 2026-08-22)** (planned 2026-07-04 from [context/post-v1-roadmap.md](../context/post-v1-roadmap.md)). Sequencing is **subscription-driven**: Weeks 1–3 extract everything that needs the expiring Snowflake (lapses within days) and Azure (~2026-07-25) subscriptions, then wind down gracefully; Weeks 4–6 run the roadmap's recommended opening sequence (Theme-1 `schema_drift` + `anomaly` → scale-aware execution G-b → incident/lineage design G-d — the G-d design half, #596, was pulled forward and done in W3, 2026-07-10) on cloud-independent infra; W7 is the stretch/burn-down buffer. See [Cycle plan](#cycle-plan--v11-6-weeks--stretch-2026-07-04--2026-08-22) below. |
| **Open issues** | **45** open repo-wide / **28** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PRs [#1283](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1283)/[#1287](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1287)/[#1288](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1288) merged (each filed and closed its own issue — #1282/#1286/#1285 — in the same session, so the count is unmoved) and earlier after PR [#1276](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1276) merged, closing [#1273](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1273) (`decimal.Decimal` values in a failed range/threshold check on a Snowflake/UC NUMERIC column crashed the whole result's JSONB insert — `sanitize_json` had no `Decimal` branch — silently discarding the entire run's results; found live during a real-user pre-deploy QA pass against Snowflake `RETAIL.ORDERS_HEADER`, confirmed **pre-existing** in already-deployed prod commit `7018d772`, not a regression. Fixed by mirroring the existing numpy/pandas coercion pattern in `backend/app/core/jsonsafe.py`; 3 new unit tests, each mutation-verified to fail for the right reason against the unfixed code; live-reproduced end-to-end pre- and post-fix against real Snowflake data) — offset by filing [#1274](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1274) (Iceberg connection over S3-compatible storage, e.g. MinIO: pyarrow's `S3FileSystem` gets `ACCESS_DENIED` reading table metadata using the same credentials the connection's own Test Connection and the sibling boto3-based `s3` connection type both accept; Test Connection never actually reads a table, so this is invisible until a real run. Scoped to S3-compatible Iceberg backends — DataQ's own Azure prod uses ADLS-backed Iceberg, likely unaffected) and [#1275](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1275) (three antd v6 deprecation console warnings — `Modal.maskClosable`, `Select.onDropdownVisibleChange`, `Drawer.width` — cosmetic, batch-fixable). All three findings came from the same session's real-user Playwright QA pass (2 fresh OTP users, all 4 datasource types, deliberate PASS/FAIL/ERROR + edge-case scenarios) ahead of a prod deploy of the 56-commit `7018d772..1758cf8a` delta; that pass also confirmed [#1208](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1208) (RunDetail Observed-column bounding) holds and that [#1184](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1184)'s own fix is unrelated to what the user was still seeing in prod — #1184 was already deployed; #1208, its follow-up correction for `schema_drift`/`comparison` observed values, was merged but not yet deployed, which is what was actually stretching. (Previous — **30** open repo-wide / **26** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PRs [#1263](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1263) (closes [#1228](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1228)), [#1265](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1265) (closes [#1221](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1221)), [#1268](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1268) (closes [#1253](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1253)), [#1269](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1269) (closes [#1230](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1230)), and [#1271](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1271) (closes [#1251](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1251)) all merged — five closes offset by filing [#1266](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1266) (the #1221 review's deferred driver-guard finding — `connect_args`'s psycopg2-specific keys have no driver-family guard, a pre-existing gap #1221 amplified rather than introduced) and [#1270](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1270) (the #1251 review's repo-wide SecretStore-fake sweep follow-up — corrected from an initial 10-file scope to ~31 files after a second review pass found the first undercounted by roughly 2x). **#1228** (merged earlier this session, its docs recount deferred to this batch — the two remaining lineage abort-instead-of-descend sites in the Snowflake pull, `_from_access_history`'s bare `raise` and a floor-failure-after-successful-traversal path, now skip just the affected tier and return the traversal's own edges as a degraded non-prunable result instead of discarding real observed lineage). **#1221** (DB pool keepalives): a warm pooled connection surviving a silent network partition could hang a read forever — `pool_pre_ping`'s own `SELECT 1` has no OS-level floor under it. Fixed with TCP keepalives (`keepalives_idle`/`interval`/`count`) on the shared engine's `connect_args`, one layer under #1102's `connect_timeout`. Review found the migrate-job engine (`alembic/env.py`, its own independent engine, exposed to the same gap and test-enforced-parity-tracked per its own docstring) hadn't been mirrored — fixed same-PR with a matching AST regression test; the driver-guard gap was deferred to #1266 above rather than fixed inline, to keep the PR focused. **#1253** (`observed_value` retention sweep): `purge_expired_sample_failures` scrubbed `sample_failures` but never the sibling list-shaped `observed_value` JSONB — correctly redacted on every read since #1252, but persisting indefinitely with no PII-minimization sweep. Fixed with a shared `_purge_column` helper reused across both columns. **#1230** (PII classifier evidence-window, option 2 chosen): the #1196 sample cap narrowed the classifier's evidence to 20 rows at capture time for pandas-backed datasources, which can flip a genuinely-PII column to "not PII" on a noisy 20-row window. Fixed by persisting a compact per-column `value_signal_summary` (5 small ints) over the FULL pre-cap population alongside the capped rows, which the classifier prefers when present and validates before trusting (rejects a summary with an inflated/inconsistent sub-count). A `/code-review` round live-verified a real crash — `_valid_summary`'s except clause didn't catch `OverflowError`, so a persisted JSONB summary with a huge float (`"n": 1e400` → `inf`) 500'd the entire read path instead of degrading to "no summary" — and found the summary wasn't threaded into the sibling `partial_unexpected_list`'s redaction (only `unexpected_index_list`'s), leaving a column masked on one list still shown on the other for the same run; both fixed and mutation-checked same-PR. **#1251** (consolidate hand-rolled `SecretStore` test doubles): five files each hand-rolled a near-identical class implementing the `SecretStore` Protocol, folded into one shared `backend/tests/support/fake_secret_store.py::FakeSecretStore`. The migration surfaced a real bug along the way — FastAPI's dependency-override resolution introspects the override CALLABLE's own signature, so a bare class (not a lambda) with constructor params, even all-defaulted ones, gets those params bound as request-level params and corrupts body validation for the endpoint under test; a bare `_WriteFailStore()` override was making `POST /connections` 422 instead of ever reaching the route. Review found the fix was patched inline at only the two call sites that hit it rather than encoded at the seam — promoted into a shared `override_secret_store(app, store)` helper (documented in the module docstring) in a same-PR follow-up commit, and `test_admin.py`'s pre-existing `_with_store` now delegates to it instead of duplicating the same lambda wrap. (Previous — **44** open repo-wide / **27** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PR [#1260](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1260) merged, closing [#1226](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1226) — net unchanged, offset by filing [#1261](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1261). **#1226**: when every alert channel failed, `CompositePublisher._fan_out_delivered_first` logged a full traceback per failing channel and then the caller (`dispatch.py::publish_connection_health`, `main.py::_poll_staleness_loop`) logged the SAME last-channel traceback a second time via its own bare `except Exception:`. Fixed with a plain marker attribute (`mark_already_logged`/`was_already_logged` in `alerting/base.py`, the same stash-on-the-object technique already used by `celery_app.py`'s `_REQUEST_ID_RESET_ATTR`) the composite sets on the re-raised error, so both callers downgrade to a warning for an error the composite already reported, while anything the composite never saw still gets a full traceback. Two full `/code-review` rounds (8 agents total) found zero correctness defects — three concrete "could this fail" scenarios (setattr on `__slots__`-based exceptions, marker loss across the `asyncio.to_thread` hop, exception-identity loss via re-wrapping) were each traced and ruled out with evidence, not assumed away — but did surface real polish gaps, all fixed same-PR: the downgraded warning in `main.py` carried zero identifying fields (now carries `error_type`); a comment overstated what `run_poll_staleness_check` does with the exception (it never catches it — corrected); a test file had invented a THIRD near-identical "channel that raises" double instead of reusing the one two files over (deduped); and a `# pragma: no cover` on the except block had gone stale now that both branches are directly tested (removed, verified via a real coverage run that both lines are hit). One idea deliberately deferred rather than acted on: centralizing the downgrade in the structlog processor chain (the CLAUDE.md §10 "redact at the logger, not the call site" precedent) — reasonable for 3+ callers, premature for the 2 that exist today — filed as #1261. (Previous — **44** open repo-wide / **27** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after PR [#1258](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1258) merged, closing [#1242](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1242) (Snowflake's privilege-filtered `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` made a zero-table sync indistinguishable from a never-synced or healthy one — fixed with two additive columns, `inventory_sync_last_table_count` + `inventory_sync_zero_since`, giving "0 tables" its own honest, non-alarming state distinct from the N>0→0 privilege-loss transition). `/code-review` found no correctness defects (verified independently by two agents across the full previous-count × table-count × failure-interleaving truth table) — only two doc-accuracy nits (wrong PR number, overstated test count), fixed in a same-PR follow-up commit. (Previous — **45** open repo-wide / **28** in the `v1.1 Backlog` milestone, re-counted with `gh issue list` on 2026-08-09 after closing [#1030](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1030) and [#1032](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1032) (both had actually been fixed and live-verified as far back as 2026-07-27 — the harness's dbt/ADF Snowflake auth moved from password to `DATAQ_LOADER_PAT` and the two missing grants were applied and confirmed effective the same day; neither issue had ever been re-checked against `docs/ops-log.md`'s own record, so they sat open for two weeks describing already-fixed state) and filing [#1257](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1257) (the one legitimate follow-up recorded in ops-log at the time — `DATAQ_LOADER`'s account-wide `MANAGE GRANTS` should be narrowed to the two-schema need — that had never been promoted to its own tracked issue). (Previous — **29** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone (46 open repo-wide as of 2026-08-09, re-counted with `gh issue list` AFTER PR [#1252](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1252) (closed [#1229](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1229)) and PR [#1255](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1255) (closed [#1254](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1254)) both merged — net unchanged (46), because closing #1229 (-1) was offset by filing [#1253](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1253) (+1, retention-sweep gap below) and #1254 was filed-then-closed same session (net 0). **#1229** (`results.observed_value` unbounded/unredacted for set-oriented GX expectations, e.g. `expect_column_distinct_values_to_be_in_set` — every distinct value a high-cardinality column ever saw persisted with no cap and no column-redaction, unlike `sample_failures` which #1196 already covered) was fixed by #1252: a capture-time cap (`gx_runner._bounded_observed_value`, reusing `SAMPLE_ROW_CAP`) plus read-time classification/redaction (`run_service.redact_observed_value` gained a `tested_column` param, threaded through the 3 read paths — `GET /runs/{id}`, the alert builder, `/mcp`'s `get_suite_results`) that classifies over the FULL persisted list before capping what's emitted, matching the established `redact_sample_failures` pattern; kept consistent with #1203's already-merged handling of the adjacent `{"error": ...}` branch in the same function. `/code-review`'s 5-agent pass found nothing above the 80-confidence bar — two sub-80 items (a doc overclaim, fixed in-PR; the retention-sweep scope question, filed as #1253 rather than scope-crept in) were still acted on per CLAUDE.md §11. Mutation-checked: reverted just the two source files, confirmed all new tests fail for the right reason, restored the fix. **#1253** (filed, open, `v1.1 Backlog`): `purge_expired_sample_failures` only scrubs `sample_failures`, never `observed_value` — a list-shaped `observed_value` is now correctly redacted on every READ (#1252) but the raw JSONB persists indefinitely with no PII-minimization sweep, unlike its sibling column. Deliberately NOT folded into #1252 — the original #1229 issue's own suggested fix shape asked only for the cap + redaction halves. **#1254** (filed AND closed same session, via #1255): CI on #1252 hit a *pre-existing, unrelated* flaky Vitest test — `SuiteForm.test.tsx`'s "reopens an existing batch target in batch mode" test renders a form whose target is `active` from first mount, so the real 400ms preview debounce (#1193) fires; the test never mocked `previewBatchTarget`'s resolution (unlike siblings that do), so when CI load let the timer win the race against RTL's unmount cleanup, the un-implemented `vi.fn()` returned `undefined` and `.then()` on `undefined` threw — `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'then') at Timeout._onTimeout SuiteForm.tsx:387:9`. Confirmed unrelated to #1252 (its diff is backend-only) and confirmed NOT a one-off — a first CI retry reproduced the identical failure, ruling out "just a flake, retry past it." Root-caused precisely (two more sibling tests in the same describe block had the identical latent exposure, not just the one that happened to fail) and reproduced deterministically pre-fix via a scratch forced-delay experiment that threw the exact CI error, then fixed all three vulnerable tests by mocking `previewBatchTarget`'s resolution, matching the idiom used elsewhere in the file. Merged as #1255, then merged into #1252's branch so its CI could go green. Two `/code-review` rounds caught six defects, and the first was the one that mattered: **`GET /orchestration/near-misses` shipped auth-only**, by analogy to its `/orchestration/pipelines` neighbour. The analogy was wrong — `pipeline_runs` is workspace-wide orchestrator telemetry with no suite-ownership concept, whereas a near-miss is derived *wholly* from `trigger_binding` rows, which are suite-owned config the sibling `GET /trigger-bindings` already scopes. As written, any signed-in user could enumerate the `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, binding_env)` of bindings on suites they cannot see. It now applies the same `accessible_suite_ids` filter, with `include_all` for a workspace admin. Three more were honesty-of-display: the panel picked the FIRST matching near-miss with `.find()`, so a second live mismatch on the same binding — two orchestrator connections reporting one DAG id against two different wrong envs, i.e. literally the #1186 ambiguity the feature exists to catch — was hidden behind the first; a failed near-miss fetch rendered identically to "no mismatch", so an outage read as healthy on the very screen built to surface it (the ADR-0039 lesson, in a new place); and the tooltip asserted the present tense ("runs keep landing in X … this binding has not fired and won't") for anything inside the 48h window while `updated_at` was fetched, typed, threaded through and never rendered — so a binding fixed an hour ago kept being told it was still broken. The last two were process: the tests drove the write LEAF rather than `orchestration_service._record_env_near_misses`, where the hashed tuple is actually *chosen*, so a change there could have desynced read from write and shipped green (a round-trip test through the real write path now covers it); and four new `assert client.get(...)` calls would have been deleted whole by `python -O` — caught by the #787 `test_assert_hygiene` guard, which is exactly what it is for. **CI caught one more that three green local runs did not**: splitting the near-miss resilience assertions into two `it`s failed the shared frontend run with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'then')` AFTER all 92 files reported green — a late effect re-invoking the cleared mock. The file's own docstring had documented that exact hazard; the lesson recorded is to check the **exit code**, not the "N passed" line.))))))) |
